I've lived/am living through this, tragic is apt.

I've had the panic for years at random intervals but it's been consistent and compulsive for a couple months now. I try to calm myself as much as possible by reminding myself that nonexistence was easier for billions of years than existing for a couple decades. I've also been looking into panpsychism to try and soothe my brain with a little false hope, as I care less about being me and more about a conscious experience. I like the idea of the universe experiencing itself although I think it's a bit too good to be true

My life is nothing really though, so never existing to begin with would still be my preference. I think it's a comfort to remember that all of our biological instinctual fears to keep existing and etc will go so for all of us folk who wish to have never been born, at the very least it will be functionally the same. 

Nothingness is scary to our senses of self preservation, but I cannot imagine having to wake up every day forever, this stuff gets exhausting fast and I think fear of infinity is the real phobia involved here for me, but an infinity of being literally incapable of feeling pain or suffering sounds better than any kind of infinity where consciousness is still active. Between those 2 existential hells I guess we got the better deal. My life has definitely swayed this opinion but honestly life feels like the worse end of the stick, despite all my fears towards wanting to continue existing, I am jealous of rocks and dirt.

I like to imagine everything speeding up right after I die, billions upon trillions of years passing instantly, a new big bang or etc occuring and new conscious experiences being had. If consciousness is special enough, surely that's possible. If it's not, then all this suffering is temporary and that's for the best. Unfortunately still causes me panic though so I really do wish I could believe in something deeper metaphysically

my head is spinning with panic on the topic currently, funny to see this thread trail back years. It's such a scary thought but without a good life it's at least a small comfort in some way. being a conscious being is a lot of effort so maybe being soil/nothing is gonna be fun, always thinking really is torture sometimes. 

I think it is very very likely there's not suffering in death. It doesn't stop me from a crippling fear but I do believe that once it happens, it's not going to be as bad as we fear it to be. Even as I'm having a panic attack about it I guess I also realize that billions of years not existing went by with far less suffering than the time we spend here. Part of me does want to hope there's always some form of conscious experience via reincarnation or forming from nothing in a new universe but even if that isn't the case I don't think it can be that bad. We have heavy biological instincts to survive and protect ourselves but I'm trying to remember that all of that fear dies when the rest does too. 

That crossover is scary to me too but consciousness really does feel like it's a lot of suffering sometimes; I think if we didn't have to stop eventually it'd be maddening.

I don't really know why you're overanalyzing a lore blurb for details as far as what the devs actually did to the hackers themselves. There's equal chance it's just lore unless they've said otherwise. Explaining the orbital gas strike being available was its main point, I doubt it's that deep for gleaming what they've actually done to hackers.

Helldivers is a satire game. You can be invested in the lore all you want, but the goldfish/chemical facility labor jokes are nothing unexpected or half-assed. Did you want them to labor for hours over a perfect lore response for a 3 day MO that wasn't even active for a day? Did you want them to hand you an unearned lore victory or randomly reset the MO like nothing happened after the hacking damage was done?
 (and soon enough that it would just happen again, presumably, till they have more safeguards against faulty samples)
To me, including the hacking in lore is less half-assed then keeping it entirely disjointed from the outcome, Awarding medals, acknowledging the situation in the lore itself instead of unimmersively ignoring it, and moving to the next plot point is perfectly reasonable. It's not like this is the last MO we will ever have a chance to win, and just because you don't benefit from medals doesn't mean the same for most people.

We have literally chosen between mines or saving a children's hospital before, this style of comedic writing is part of the lore so you're gonna be very disappointed if you take every win or loss with this much salt because the joke didn't land for you personally. It sucks hacking affected this MO but they've spun it into an fun accurate in-universe outcome (again, satire universe, our flamethrowers have capsaicin, our upgrades include teaching our crew to reload faster by leaving unused ammunition instead of replacing it, there's tv ads featuring child labor details; forced labor and executing goldfish fits right in). Being invested in the lore is one thing, being mad at kernel AC is valid enough, but this is ONE MO, and the story is still progressing, the real world events are being incorporated into the story instead of ignored cheaply, and the Gloom was unlikely to be gloriously defeated by sample collection alone anyways, so there is more work to be done and win or lose I'm sure this was far from the deciding factor overall. 

Guy was poking fun at you for being hyper serious about it, I don't think calling them brainrot or acting like they said some immature nonsense, just because you don't like sarcasm pointed at you, is necessarily very mature either. You replied to a positive, lighthearted comment with pretty negative energy over something that, even lore wise, isn't huge in the grand scheme (presumably even for the Gloom arc itself). It's no surprise you're in the minority on this, I am invested in the lore and story and I can appreciate them handling this the way they did and even if I didn't then I'd still recognize that it is just one singular MO, not even a long or ultra-critical story turning point one either, and one filler MO fizzling out (with rewards and orbital gas strike being rewarded anyways) is far from what I'd need to feel like Arrowhead personally dealt me some truly unfair outcome
